question: Three capacitors of capacitances $2\,\mu\text{F}$, $4\,\mu\text{F}$ and $6\,\mu\text{F}$ are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent capacitance. Explain why the equivalent capacitance is greater than each individual capacitance.

options.A: $C_{\text{eq}}=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{6}=\frac{11}{12}\,\mu\text{F}$; it is smaller because capacitors are in series
options.B: $C_{\text{eq}}=2+4+6=12\,\mu\text{F}$; it exceeds each capacitor because, at the same potential difference, charges stored by all parallel branches add
options.C: $C_{\text{eq}}=6\,\mu\text{F}$ because the largest capacitor determines the combination
options.D: $C_{\text{eq}}=1\,\mu\text{F}$ because capacitances in parallel are added reciprocally
